plan: Fill the graveyard, sacrifice creatures for value, and bring the best of them back with Meren every end step.

review.text:
HOW THE DECK WINS. It does not win by attacking; it wins by making every death profitable and then out-attriting the table.

Turns 1-3: the cheap engine pieces. Viscera Seer and Carrion Feeder are one-mana sacrifice outlets that turn any creature into scry 1 or a +1/+1 counter. Stitcher's Supplier mills three when it enters and three more when it dies, Spore Frog and Sakura-Tribe Elder are bodies that want to die, and Gravecrawler recasts itself from the graveyard as long as you control a Zombie. Grisly Salvage, Mulch and Life from the Loam fill the yard early rather than develop the board. Then Meren at four mana.

Turns 4-6: this is where setup meets cash-in. The setup half is the sacrifice outlets plus the cheap recurring bodies; the cash-in half is the death triggers - Grim Haruspex and Midnight Reaper draw on each nontoken creature you lose, Blood Artist and Zulaport Cutthroat drain, Grave Pact and Dictate of Erebos make each of your deaths strip a creature from every opponent. Meren's end-step trigger returns a creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield if its mana value is at most your experience counters, and otherwise to your hand - so each early death both pays for the next return and raises the ceiling of what you can return. Fleshbag Marauder, Plaguecrafter and Ravenous Chupacabra are the engine's favourite reanimation targets: removal that comes back.

Turns 7 and on: the top end. Butcher of Malakir, Massacre Wurm, Moldgraf Monstrosity and Woodfall Primus - with Victimize, Dread Return, Animate Dead, Necromancy and Living Death to cheat them in ahead of their cost. Living Death is the haymaker: after a game of self-mill and sacrifice it sweeps the opponents' boards and rebuilds yours. What actually ends the game is usually Blood Artist and Zulaport Cutthroat draining out while Grave Pact or Butcher of Malakir empties the table, or a reanimated top-end beater once nobody can block.

CURVE AGAINST LANDS AND RAMP. Average mana value is 3.03, and the curve clusters hard in the middle: 18 cards at 2 and 22 at 3, against 4 at 4, 6 at 5, 2 at 6, 2 at 7 and 1 at 8. That is a cheap deck, and Lands is at 37 against a target of 38 - appropriate. The problem is Ramp at 5 against a target of 10. With only Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Golgari Signet, Cultivate and Sakura-Tribe Elder, turn-four Meren depends on hitting land drops, and the 5-to-8 slots arrive on schedule rather than early. Meren herself does the cheating later, but the first Meren cast is the deck's most important turn and nothing accelerates toward it.

COLOUR. Black is at 58 pips with 24 sources; green at 27 pips with 21 sources. Black is clearly the primary colour, and cards like Grave Pact at {1}{B}{B}{B} and Massacre Wurm at {3}{B}{B}{B} want more than one black source. 24 sources for 58 pips is a little thin for triple-black.

WHEN THE COMMANDER IS ANSWERED. Better than most commander-centric decks. Meren is the engine, but Animate Dead, Necromancy, Victimize, Dread Return and Living Death all reanimate without her, and Bloodghast, Gravecrawler, Golgari Grave-Troll and Stinkweed Imp return themselves. Card advantage is at 11 against 12 and most of it - Grim Haruspex, Midnight Reaper, Harvester of Souls, Fecundity, Deathreap Ritual - keys off creatures dying, not off Meren. You lose tempo and the recursion engine, not the deck. Note Meren costs {2}{B}{G} and recasting her each time she is answered taxes a deck already short on ramp.

CATEGORIES. Targeted disruption is at 16 against a target of 12 and Plan is at 40 against 30, while Ramp sits at 5 against 10. The heavy category is where the slack is: eight of those sixteen are one-for-one instants that do nothing with the graveyard - Doom Blade, Go for the Throat, Infernal Grasp, Murder, Hero's Downfall, Naturalize, Krosan Grip, Beast Within. Compare Shriekmaw, Acidic Slime, Reclamation Sage, Fleshbag Marauder, Plaguecrafter and Ravenous Chupacabra, which do the same job on a creature Meren can return. Mass disruption is at 5 against 6.

Two cards sit in their category only on a stretch: Viscera Seer counts in Card advantage, but scry 1 does not turn one card into more than one card - it is a sacrifice outlet that filters. And Spore Frog counts in Mass disruption as a fog; it blanks one combat step rather than dealing with many things, though with a sacrifice outlet and Meren it does that every turn.

LANDS THAT MAKE NO MANA. One: Evolving Wilds, which sacrifices itself to fetch a basic land tapped - so a Forest or a Swamp, and a landfall trigger for Bloodghast.

maybeboard.name: Wood Elves
maybeboard.why: Wood Elves is ramp on a creature body that fetches an untapped Forest (including Overgrown Tomb), feeds the sacrifice outlets and gives Meren a land every end step, in place of the narrowest one-for-one removal spell.

maybeboard.name: Yavimaya Elder
maybeboard.why: Ramp is at 5 against a target of 10 and Card advantage at 11 against 12, while Targeted disruption is at 16 against 12: Yavimaya Elder is ramp and draw on a creature that pays you for dying (two basics to hand when it dies, {2} and sacrifice to draw), in place of the most expensive plain creature-kill spell.

maybeboard.name: Skullclamp
maybeboard.why: Card advantage is at 11 against a target of 12 and Viscera Seer only counts there on a stretch: Skullclamp turns every creature that dies into two cards for one mana, which is what this deck does anyway, in place of the most redundant artifact/enchantment removal in a Targeted disruption category sitting at 16 against 12.
